name: msgpack C++ buffer unpacking (msgpack::unpack)
description:
msgpack::unpack deserializes a raw byte buffer of untrusted, attacker-controlled MessagePack-encoded data into a msgpack::object tree (object_handle). It is the primary entry point into the whole decoding stack: a one-byte type-tag dispatcher, a recursive/stack-based aggregate (array/map) state machine, and length/size-limited handlers for strings, binaries and extension types, all security-relevant because the format encodes variable-length containers and payloads directly from the wire with no inherent bound beyond the configurable unpack_limit.

- msgpack::unpack (target, const char*,len[,off][,referenced],f,user_data,limit): resolves (depending on MSGPACK_DEFAULT_API_VERSION, default 3) to v3::unpack -> v2::detail::unpack_imp -> detail::parse_imp -> detail::context<VisitorHolder>::execute, which is the core byte-tag dispatcher/state machine (msgpack/v2/parse.hpp). Internally it drives msgpack::v2::detail::create_object_visitor (msgpack/v2/create_object_visitor.hpp), whose visit_str/visit_bin/visit_ext/start_array/start_map functions build the msgpack::object tree and enforce unpack_limit.
- the sibling msgpack::unpack overloads (with std::size_t& off, bool& referenced, object_handle& result out-param, or msgpack::zone&) are variants: same core (unpack_imp/execute/create_object_visitor), different call sites/offset tracking/ownership of the output object - they exercise exactly the same decoder logic with different parameter combinations (partial decode via off, buffer-reference detection via the unpack_reference_func callback and referenced flag).
- msgpack::unpacker (class in msgpack/v2/unpack.hpp, built on parser<unpacker,...>) + its next()/reserve_buffer()/buffer()/buffer_consumed() methods: the streaming variant of the same feature - it feeds chunks of the buffer into the same detail::context<VisitorHolder>::execute core incrementally (parse one object, keep remainder, parse next), so a harness can feed fragmented/partial input and exercise the PARSE_CONTINUE/resume paths that one-shot unpack() cannot reach.
- msgpack::pack (msgpack/v1/pack.hpp, packer<Stream>::pack_*) is the inverse operation: used throughout the project's own tests (test/pack_unpack.cpp) to build the msgpack-encoded buffers that are then round-tripped through unpack(); including it lets the harness build structurally-valid-but-fuzzed inputs (nested arrays/maps/str/bin/ext of varying size) rather than only raw bytes.
- msgpack::object_handle::get().as<T>() / operator<< (object.hpp) are consumers that walk the freshly produced object tree (recursively visiting arrays/maps and converting to typed values), exercising additional code after unpack() that can trip bugs in how the zone-allocated object graph was built (e.g. malformed nested containers, dangling str/bin references when the unpack_reference_func is used).

Input space (each value below selects a different path through detail::context::execute / create_object_visitor):
- the raw MessagePack byte stream itself: type-tag byte in [0x00,0xff] selects fixint, nil/bool, float32/float64, uint8/16/32/64, int8/16/32/64, fixstr/str8/16/32, bin8/16/32, fixext1/2/4/8/16 and ext8/16/32, fixarray/array16/32, fixmap/map16/32 - varying nesting depth and declared element/byte counts is the most permissive dimension and drives the most core code (deep recursion, large declared sizes, truncated trailers that trigger PARSE_CONTINUE / insufficient_bytes).
- unpack_reference_func f + user_data: a predicate called from visit_str/visit_bin/visit_ext deciding whether the object aliases the input buffer (referenced=true) or is deep-copied into the zone - toggling it changes whether the harness must keep the input buffer alive and exercises both code paths in those visitors.
- unpack_limit (array/map/str/bin/ext/depth): lowering these from the default 0xffffffff makes array/map/str/bin/ext/depth_size_overflow exceptions reachable with small inputs, an orthogonal path worth exercising alongside the default (unbounded) limit.
- off / len: partial-buffer parsing (off > 0, len < full message) exercises PARSE_EXTRA_BYTES and PARSE_CONTINUE result handling.
This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers and tests do with the target stays.
